1.meaning: And We place / We set down / We establish — to put something in position.
1.grammar: A present/imperfect verb preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The na- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The verb means to lay down, set in place, or establish something.
1.root: و-ض-ع (w-ḍ-ʿ) — to put down, place, lay, set

2.meaning: The balances / the scales — instruments for weighing, used literally and as a metaphor for just measure and judgment.
2.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural noun. The -a ending here is accusative, the case taken by a direct object (the thing being set or placed). The singular is mīzān ('a balance'); the plural denotes weighing-scales or, figuratively, standards of justice.

3.meaning: Justice, equity, fairness — giving each thing its right measure without excess or deficiency.
3.grammar: A definite noun. The -a ending is accusative, the case often used for a direct object or for a descriptive/qualifying noun. Qisṭ denotes scrupulous fairness — balanced, exact justice.
3.root: ق-س-ط (q-s-ṭ) — to act justly, give fair measure

4.meaning: For the Day / belonging to the Day — assigning or attaching something to a particular day.
4.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition/particle li- ('for, belonging to'). The -i ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition. Yawm means a day or an appointed time/period.
4.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, appointed time

5.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
5.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.

6.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
6.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

7.meaning: It/she is wronged / treated unjustly — to have a wrong done to one, to be deprived of due or dealt with unfairly.
7.grammar: A present-tense passive verb: 'is being wronged,' the doer unnamed. The tu- prefix marks a feminine or impersonal 'it/she' as the one wronged; the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present tense.
7.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression

8.meaning: A soul, self, or person — the inner self of a living being; by extension, an individual.
8.grammar: A singular feminine noun, indefinite ('a soul'). The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamma) is the indefinite nominative case, which typically marks the subject or doer.
8.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath

9.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
9.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'
9.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — thing, to will

10.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
10.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

11.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

11.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

12.meaning: The weight or measure of something — the amount that balances against it on a scale; figuratively even the tiniest equivalent quantity.
12.grammar: A noun denoting a unit of weight: 'the weight of.' The final '-a' marks the accusative case, here typical of a noun functioning as the object of a verb. It also stands as the first term of a possessive pairing ('weight OF …'), in which a following noun is read in the genitive.
12.root: ث-ق-ل (th-q-l) — weight, heaviness; that which weighs in a balance

13.meaning: A single grain or seed, such as a kernel of grain; one small seed-unit of a plant.
13.grammar: An indefinite singular noun with the -in (tanwīn kasr) ending, marking the genitive case. The noun ends in tā' marbūṭa, which is sounded as 't' once a case-ending follows it, so the form reads 'ḥabbatin'. The genitive is the case taken after a preposition or when a noun is possessed by another ('… of a grain'); the indefiniteness gives 'a grain'.
13.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — grain, seed; also love, affection

14.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
14.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

15.meaning: Mustard — the mustard plant, proverbially cited for its tiny seed as a byword for something extremely small.
15.grammar: A noun (collective, naming the plant). The final -in is the indefinite genitive ending, the form a noun takes when indefinite and following a preposition or another noun (e.g. 'a grain of mustard'). It is famed for the minuteness of its seed.

16.meaning: We came / We brought — the first-person plural of coming, also used in the sense of bringing or producing something.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb. The attached -nā marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The verb's core sense is 'to come'; with an object it carries the sense 'to bring / to bring forth'.

17.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
17.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

18.meaning: 'And He suffices / is enough' — to be sufficient, adequate, and fully enough so that nothing more is needed. It conveys complete adequacy, often used to affirm that Allah alone is enough.
18.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a 3rd-person masculine singular perfect (past-tense) verb (Form I) whose final weak root letter (the yāʾ) appears as a long -ā. It states a completed yet timeless fact — 'and He is sufficient' — the kind of perfect form used for an enduring truth.
18.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, be enough, be adequate; to spare someone need of anything else

19.meaning: A particle 'with/for/by' joined to the word 'us'. It signals accompaniment, means, or that something concerns or befalls 'us'.
19.grammar: The preposition bi- always attaches to the front of a noun or pronoun and puts it in the genitive. Here it is fused with the attached pronoun -nā ('us'), the first-person plural object. The bi- can convey 'with', 'by means of', or that an event happens 'to/concerning' the people named.

20.meaning: Those who reckon, calculate, and take account — keepers of the tally who compute and call to account.
20.grammar: An active participle in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks a masculine plural in the object/oblique form (used when the word is a direct object, follows a preposition, or serves as a predicate). It names those who do the reckoning.
20.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to count, reckon, calculate, take account

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: 'We gave / granted / brought'. To hand over or bestow something upon someone; to come to someone with a gift or grant.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative (form IV) sense 'to bring/grant to someone'. The '-nā' suffix is the doer 'we' in completed past time. It often takes two objects — the recipient and the thing given.
2.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to give, bring

3.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
3.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)
3.root: — (proper name; non-Arabic origin)

4.meaning: A linking phrase 'and Aaron' — joining the proper name of the Prophet Hārūn with 'and'.
4.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus a proper name. It ends in -a and is a 'diptote' — a noun that does not take full case endings, so it shows -a (not -un/-in) and no nunation; this -a form covers both the object and after-a-preposition roles.

5.meaning: The criterion — that which separates and distinguishes truth from falsehood, right from wrong; a decisive standard of discrimination.
5.grammar: A definite verbal noun (maṣdar) of the fuʿlān pattern, denoting the means of separating or distinguishing. The -a ending is accusative, the case taken by a direct object. It signifies a decisive divider between truth and falsehood.

6.meaning: And a light / radiance / illumination — brightness that shines, especially light that is emitted or shed.
6.grammar: A noun preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The final -an is the indefinite accusative ending, the form an indefinite noun takes as a direct object or descriptive complement ('a light'). Ḍiyāʾ denotes shining brightness or illumination.
6.root: ض-و-أ (ḍ-w-ʾ) — to shine, give light, illuminate

7.meaning: And a reminder / remembrance — that which brings something to mind, an admonition, or the act of mentioning and recalling.
7.grammar: A verbal noun preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The final -an is the indefinite accusative ending, used for an indefinite noun functioning as object or complement ('a reminder'). Dhikr spans remembrance, mention, and admonition.
7.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

8.meaning: 'For the mindful/God-conscious ones' — for those who have taqwa: a reverent, protective awareness of Allah that makes a person guard against wrongdoing and shield themselves from His displeasure. The word names people characterized by this watchful piety.

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

8.grammar: A preposition li- ('for') joined to a definite masculine sound plural active participle. The -ina ending is the plural form used after a preposition or as an object (the oblique/genitive-accusative case) — 'for the … ones'. The participle pattern (muftaʿil) describes those who actively do the action: those who keep themselves guarded.
8.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — guarding, shielding, protecting

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: 'They fear' or 'they hold in awe' — experiencing khashya, a fear mixed with reverence and awareness of someone's greatness, especially the kind of dread that comes from knowledge of the one feared.
2.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The -awna ending marks a masculine-plural 'they' subject (the long final root-vowel blends into the plural ending) and the indicative mood, which states the action as an ongoing or habitual fact.
2.root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y) — fear blended with awe and reverence

3.meaning: Their Lord, Master, and Sustainer — 'rabb' is the one who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; with the attached pronoun, the Lord who is theirs.
3.grammar: A masculine noun with the possessive 'their' attached. The -a vowel before -hum marks the accusative case, the case typically used for the object of a verb.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, mastery

4.meaning: 'In the unseen' — the preposition 'in/by' with 'the unseen': that which is hidden from perception, beyond what the senses can reach (such as Allah, the angels, and the Hereafter). It denotes the realm one cannot directly observe yet may affirm.
4.grammar: A preposition bi- joined to a definite masculine singular noun. The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition — hence 'in the unseen'. The article al- makes it 'the unseen' as a known whole rather than 'an unseen thing'.
4.root: غ-ي-ب (gh-y-b) — being hidden, absent from sight

5.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
5.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

6.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
6.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

7.meaning: The Hour — the appointed final time: the moment of the world's ending and the Resurrection. Though literally 'an hour' (a span of time), with the definite article it denotes that singular, decisive coming Hour.
7.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'); the article's 'l' assimilates into the following 's' (heard as 'as-sāʿa'). The final -i is genitive — the case used when the word is possessed by a preceding noun ('… of the Hour') or follows a preposition.
7.root: س-و-ع (s-w-ʿ) — a passing moment or span of time; an 'hour'

8.meaning: An active participle meaning 'those who are apprehensive / fearful / full of awe and dread.' It describes people in a state of anxious, reverent fear — wary and on edge out of awe or concern over an outcome.
8.grammar: An active participle (a describing word naming the doer of an action/state) in the masculine plural, 'ones who are apprehensive.' It follows the mufʿil pattern (mu- + i-vowelled stem, mushfiq), the active participle of a form IV verb (ashfaqa). The -ūna ending marks masculine plural and the nominative case, the base case used for a subject or a descriptive predicate.
8.root: ش-ف-ق (sh-f-q) — to be apprehensive, fearful out of care or awe

1.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and this (one)' — the pointing word 'this' (for something near, masculine/neutral) joined to 'and'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to the demonstrative hādhā ('this'), used to point to something near at hand (masculine singular). A demonstrative like this has a fixed ending and does not change for grammatical case; it can stand as a subject or be linked to a following noun ('this ___').

2.meaning: A reminder, mention, or admonition — that which calls something to mind and keeps it present; remembrance, or a notice that stirs awareness.
2.grammar: A noun with the -un (indefinite nominative) ending, the case that typically marks the subject or predicate of a sentence ('a reminder'). The tanwīn (-un) signals it is indefinite ('a/some'). The word covers both calling-to-mind and the spoken mention that prompts it.
2.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — remembering, mentioning, calling to mind

3.meaning: Blessed — endowed with divine blessing (baraka), abundant and enduring goodness.
3.grammar: A passive participle of form III (mu- prefix with the -ā- pattern), meaning 'one that has been blessed.' The final -un is the indefinite nominative ending, typically used for an indefinite subject or predicate ('it is blessed'). It describes something filled with lasting, God-given goodness.
3.root: ب-ر-ك (b-r-k) — to bless; abundance and enduring good

4.meaning: 'We sent it down / revealed it'. Past-tense verb from anzala ('to send down, cause to descend'), with the 'We' of majesty as subject and 'it' as object. Characteristically used of revelation sent down from above.

parts.en: sent down / caused to descend (causative stem)

4.grammar: A past-tense verb of the causative pattern (af ʿala: 'to make come down'). The suffix -nā marks a first-person plural subject, 'we'. The attached -hu is the object 'it/him'. In divine speech the plural 'We' conveys majesty, not number.
4.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to come down, descend; (causative) to send down

5.meaning: Then is it you (who…)? — an emphatic, often reproachful question singling out the addressees: 'so are YOU the ones who…?'
5.grammar: A compound: the interrogative particle a- ('is it…?') plus the connector fa- ('then/so') prefixed to the independent pronoun antum ('you,' masculine plural). Together they form a pointed rhetorical question fronting the addressees for emphasis.
5.root: — (particles and a pronoun; no triliteral root)

6.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
6.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

7.meaning: Deniers, rejecters — those who refuse to acknowledge something, treating it as objectionable or false.
7.grammar: An active participle of form IV in the masculine sound plural. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the subject/nominative form ('the ones who reject'). It names those who disavow or refuse to recognize something as true or proper.
7.root: ن-ك-ر (n-k-r) — to deny, disavow, reject, find objectionable

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: 'We gave / granted / brought'. To hand over or bestow something upon someone; to come to someone with a gift or grant.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative (form IV) sense 'to bring/grant to someone'. The '-nā' suffix is the doer 'we' in completed past time. It often takes two objects — the recipient and the thing given.
2.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to give, bring

3.meaning: The proper name Ibrāhīm (the Prophet Abraham).
3.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -a ending here serves for both accusative and genitive because the name is a diptote — a class of nouns that refuses tanwīn (no -an/-in) and uses a single -a for these two cases. So this one -a covers 'Ibrāhīm' whether as an object or as 'of Ibrāhīm'.
3.root: — (proper name)

4.meaning: His right guidance / his sound judgment / his maturity — the correct direction, integrity, and good sense belonging to him.
4.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive -hu ('his'). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the case taken by a direct object (the thing given or attained). Rushd denotes rightness of conduct, mature good sense, and being well-guided.
4.root: ر-ش-د (r-sh-d) — to be rightly guided, of sound judgment, mature

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
6.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
6.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

7.meaning: And we were / we used to be — the past-tense of 'to be' with a 'we' subject; often expresses a continuous or habitual past state ('we used to').
7.grammar: The past-tense verb 'to be' prefixed with 'wa-' ('and'). The suffix '-nā' marks a first-person plural subject ('we'); its nūn assimilates into the doubled nūn of the stem 'kunn-' (shown by the shadda), so only the long vowel is written, but the full ending is '-nā'. It describes a state in the completed past.
7.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

8.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
8.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

9.meaning: Knowers — those who know; possessors of knowledge and full awareness.
9.grammar: An active participle in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks a masculine plural in the object/oblique form (used as a direct object, after a preposition, or as a predicate). It names those who possess knowledge.
9.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge, awareness

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

2.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
2.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

3.meaning: To / for his father — the noun 'father' attached to a possessive 'his' and preceded by the preposition 'to/for.'
3.grammar: Preposition + noun + possessive pronoun. The li- prefix means 'to' or 'for.' 'Father' is one of a small group of nouns that show case with a long vowel: the -ī here reflects the genitive required after the preposition. The attached -hi means 'his' (its 'i' vowel harmonizes after the preceding -ī).
3.root: ا-ب-و (ʾ-b-w) — fatherhood; father

4.meaning: And his people / his folk / his kinfolk — the community or nation to which a person belongs, plus 'his.'
4.grammar: A noun preceded by the connector wa- ('and') and carrying the possessive -hi ('his'). The -i ending is genitive; here it appears because of the attached possessive pronoun (a noun linked to a following possessor stands in the genitive). Qawm denotes a people, tribe, or community.
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people who stand together

5.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

6.meaning: This (feminine) — a pointing word ('this one here') used for a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
6.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand. It is fixed in form and does not change for case; it commonly precedes the noun it points to.

7.meaning: The statues / images / likenesses — fashioned figures and representations, such as carved idols or sculpted forms.
7.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence ('the statues…'). The singular is timthāl ('a statue / likeness'); the word denotes crafted images or figures.
7.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — to resemble; likeness, image, representation

8.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
8.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

9.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
9.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

10.meaning: 'For it / to it, belonging to it' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a pronoun referring to a feminine singular thing; it expresses possession or benefit ('it has / it gets').
10.grammar: Preposition 'li-' (here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun) plus an attached object pronoun. The -hā suffix means 'it/her,' a feminine singular. Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -hā is a fixed form and does not change shape.
10.root: — (preposition + pronoun)

11.meaning: Ones who are devotedly secluded; those keeping to a place in constant, focused retreat and worship.
11.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) in the masculine sound plural. The -ūna ending marks a plural group in the nominative case, the form used for the subject or for naming who/what something is.
11.root: ع-ك-ف (ʿ-k-f) — to cling to, keep to a place, devote oneself in retreat

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: 'We found / came upon / discovered' — to find something, either by encountering it or by determining it to be in a certain state.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with the '-nā' ending meaning 'we'. So it means 'we found' or 'we came upon'. The '-nā' suffix attached to the past-tense stem marks the doers as a 'we' (first-person plural).
2.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to come upon, to discover

3.meaning: 'Our fathers / forefathers / ancestors.' The plural of 'father,' denoting forebears and the line of those who came before, with the attached 'our' marking them as one's own ancestry.
3.grammar: A plural noun ('fathers') with the attached possessive -nā ('our'). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the case typically used to mark the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or certain adverbial roles.
3.root: أ-ب-و (ʾ-b-w) — father, fatherhood

4.meaning: 'For it / to it, belonging to it' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a pronoun referring to a feminine singular thing; it expresses possession or benefit ('it has / it gets').
4.grammar: Preposition 'li-' (here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun) plus an attached object pronoun. The -hā suffix means 'it/her,' a feminine singular. Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -hā is a fixed form and does not change shape.
4.root: — (preposition + pronoun)

5.meaning: Worshippers; servants who devote themselves in worship and humble obedience. This is the masculine plural active participle 'those who worship/serve', in the accusative/genitive form.
5.grammar: Active participle (Form I, fāʿil pattern), sound masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the accusative or genitive case of a masculine plural, signalling 'more than two' and typically functioning as an object, or following a preposition or oath particle.
5.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, devote oneself in obedience

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
2.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

3.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
3.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

4.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
4.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

5.meaning: 'And your forefathers' — joins with 'and' the noun 'fathers/ancestors' bound to the possessor 'your (plural).' 'Ābā'' denotes fathers and, by extension, forebears.
5.grammar: Begins with the connective 'wa' ('and'). 'Ābā'u' is the broken plural of 'ab' (father), here with the '-u' nominative ending that marks it as a subject or as a noun joined to one. The attached '-kum' is the possessive 'your' (masculine plural). So: 'and your fathers/ancestors.'

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
6.root: — (particle)

7.meaning: Means 'straying / error / being lost' — wandering off the right path, the opposite of guidance, whether literally losing one's way or going astray in belief and conduct.
7.grammar: An abstract noun: 'straying / error.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite) — the case a noun takes after a preposition or in a possessive link, e.g. 'in an error.' The long -ā- belongs to this noun-pattern.
7.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

8.meaning: Means 'clear / plain / making manifest' — something that is evident in itself and also makes other things plain, leaving no ambiguity.
8.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) from a pattern that often carries the sense 'making clear' as well as 'being clear.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite), the form taken after a preposition or when describing a genitive noun — i.e. it agrees with a preceding indefinite noun in the genitive ('a clear …').
8.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct; to make evident

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: "have you come to us?" — the question-marker "?" plus the past-tense verb "you came/arrived," with "us" as the destination.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb fronted by the interrogative particle a- ("is it that…?"). The -ta ending marks a single male "you" as the doer of the completed action; the suffix -nā is the object "us."

3.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
3.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
3.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

4.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

4.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.
4.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

5.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
5.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

6.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
6.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

7.meaning: Those who play, jest, or amuse themselves; people occupied with idle sport rather than serious purpose. This is the masculine plural active participle in the accusative/genitive form, carrying the definite article 'the'.
7.grammar: Active participle (Form I, fāʿil pattern) with the definite article 'al-', sound masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the accusative or genitive case of a masculine plural and indicates a group, typically as an object of a verb or after a preposition.
7.root: ل-ع-ب (l-ʿ-b) — to play, jest, sport, amuse oneself

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: A particle of retraction and transition meaning 'rather,' 'on the contrary,' or 'nay.' It cancels or sets aside what was just said and corrects course toward a truer statement that follows — turning the listener from one idea to another.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes its ending). It functions to retract or override the preceding statement and introduce a correction or contrast — 'no, rather …'

3.meaning: Your Lord. 'Rabb' means the Lord who creates, owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs all that He has made; combined with 'your' (plural) it addresses a group as 'the Lord of you all.'
3.grammar: A noun 'Lord' with the possessive -kum ('your,' addressing more than one person). The -u before the suffix is the nominative case marker, the form typically used when the word is the subject of a sentence.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, ownership, sustaining

4.meaning: The Lord of — owner, master and sustainer who creates, possesses and governs. Of Allah it names the One who brings up and maintains all that exists.
4.grammar: The noun 'rabb' with the final -u marking the nominative case (subject or predicate: '… is the Lord'). Standing before a following noun it carries the sense 'Lord of …'. It combines ownership, authority and nurturing care.
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing

5.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
5.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

6.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
6.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.
6.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land

7.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

8.meaning: He originated/created them (a feminine or non-rational plural group) from nothing, bringing them into existence. A past-tense verb of creating, with an attached object pronoun 'them'.
8.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he did' the action, completed. The attached -hunna is the object pronoun 'them', referring to a feminine plural or a plural of non-rational things.
8.root: ف-ط-ر (f-ṭ-r) — to split open, to originate, to bring into existence for the first time

9.meaning: And I — the standalone first-person singular pronoun 'I,' here joined by 'and.' As a detached pronoun it stands on its own (typically as subject), unlike the attached endings.
9.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and.' 'anā' is the independent (detached) pronoun 'I,' used for emphasis or to begin/identify the subject; it does not take a case ending and is fixed in form.
9.root: — (pronoun, no root)

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

11.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' addressed to a group of people (plural 'you'). It points to something at a distance — whether physical, or to a previously mentioned matter — and is directed at multiple listeners.
11.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for something distant. The base 'dhā' carries the sense 'that', the 'li' is an element of distance, and the ending '-kum' tells you the speaker is addressing a plural 'you' — it specifies the audience, not the thing pointed at. It does not change for case.

12.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
12.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

13.meaning: 'The witnesses / those who testify' — people who observe and bear testimony, affirming the truth of something.
13.grammar: al- is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'sh', heard as ash-shā…). The active participle shāhid ('one who witnesses') takes the sound masculine plural ending -īna, which makes it plural and marks the accusative/genitive case — typically the object of a verb, or the object of a preposition, or part of a possessive phrase.
13.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, to testify, to be present

1.meaning: By Allah — an oath sworn upon the name of Allah. The phrase is built from two oath particles together: the wāw of oath followed by the tāʾ of oath, the latter used almost exclusively with the name Allah and conveying added emphasis or wonder.
1.grammar: An oath construction. Both the wāw (wāw al-qasam) and the tāʾ (tāʾ al-qasam) are oath particles meaning 'by'; neither is the coordinating conjunction 'and'. An oath particle puts the following noun in the genitive, hence the -i ending on 'Allah'. The whole phrase introduces a solemn promise or affirmation.

2.meaning: I will surely scheme/plot against; I am absolutely determined to devise a plan. The verb means to contrive a clever or covert stratagem. It is emphatic and future-oriented, with an opening emphasis and a heavy concluding emphasis attached.

parts.en: I scheme / plot (stem akīd- + pre-nūn vowel -a)

2.grammar: Present/future verb, first-person singular ('I…'), made doubly emphatic: the prefixed 'la-' and the suffixed heavy 'nūn of emphasis' (-nna) together turn it into a forceful vow, 'I will most certainly…'. The 'a-' prefix marks the first-person singular. The verb stem is akīd-; before the heavy nūn the indicative -u is replaced by the juncture vowel -a, so the -a belongs to the pre-nūn environment, not to the stem.
2.root: ك-ي-د (k-y-d) — to plot, scheme, devise a stratagem

3.meaning: Your idols — the carved images or statues set up as objects of worship. A masculine plural noun in the accusative (as an object) with the attached possessive 'your' (addressing a group).
3.grammar: Noun, broken plural, in the accusative case (the -a before the suffix marks it as a direct object). The attached -kum means 'your', addressing a plural 'you'.
3.root: ص-ن-م (ṣ-n-m) — idol, carved image set up for worship

4.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
4.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
4.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

5.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
5.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'you turn (yourselves), face, or direct yourselves toward' — to orient oneself in a direction.
6.grammar: A present-tense Form II verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all turn'). The plural marker '-ū' appears without the indicative '-na', showing the jussive/subjunctive mood — fitting after a conditional particle ('wherever you turn…').
6.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to turn, be near, take charge, face toward

7.meaning: Turning one's back, going away, retreating; people in the act of departing. This is the masculine plural active participle of 'to turn away', in the accusative/genitive form, often describing the manner in which people leave.
7.grammar: Active participle of a Form IV verb (ʾafʿala), following the mufʿil participle pattern, sound masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the accusative or genitive of a masculine plural; as an accusative it commonly functions as a circumstantial description ('while turning away').
7.root: د-ب-ر (d-b-r) — the back, hind part; to turn the back, to go away

1.meaning: So he made/rendered them; he turned them into (some state). A past-tense verb that can take two objects, meaning 'to make something become something'. Here it carries the attached object 'them', preceded by the connector 'then/so'.
1.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he did', completed). The prefixed 'fa-' means 'so/then', marking sequence or consequence. The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them' (masculine plural).
1.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, place, bring into a state

2.meaning: Fragments, broken pieces, bits smashed apart. An indefinite noun naming the result of breaking something into many small parts, in the accusative form.
2.grammar: Noun in the accusative case with nunation (the '-an' ending), marking it as indefinite and typically functioning as an object or as a description of the result of an action.
2.root: ج-ذ-ذ (j-dh-dh) — to cut off, break into pieces, fragment

3.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
3.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
3.root: — (particle)

4.meaning: Large, great, big, or major — an adjective describing something of great size, amount, or importance. It can also mean elder/older in age. The -an ending leaves it indefinite ('a large …').
4.grammar: An indefinite adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn): it commonly marks the object of a verb, or works adverbially, and signals the word is indefinite ('a large one'). It pairs with ṣaghīr ('small').
4.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, largeness, being great or old

5.meaning: 'For them / to them / theirs' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the pronoun 'them,' expressing that something pertains, belongs, or is owed to that group.
5.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to'), whose vowel becomes -a before an attached pronoun, joined to -hum ('them'). It commonly expresses possession or benefit — 'theirs / for them.' Particles like this carry no case or tense of their own.

6.meaning: 'So that they may / perhaps they will.' A particle expressing hope, expectation, or purpose, fused with the pronoun 'them'; it introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

6.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps, in the hope that, so that') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), which serves as its subject. Laʿalla belongs to a family of particles that put a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -hum is that fixed object form. It conveys hope or an intended purpose rather than certainty.
6.root: — (particle with pronoun; no root)

7.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
7.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

8.meaning: To return, go back, or turn back — to come back to a place, state, or point of origin. Used of a group: 'they return / come back'.
8.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they return'). The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks an ongoing or repeated action by a group of males or a mixed group. The -ūna 'indicative' ending appears when nothing precedes the verb to shorten it.
8.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — returning, going back, repetition

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
2.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

3.meaning: He did / he acted / he committed — he carried out a deed. A general verb for performing or bringing about an action.

parts.en: he did / did it (he/it, masculine singular, past)

3.grammar: A simple past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular. The third-person masculine singular has no separate suffix; the bare stem ending in -a expresses 'he did' as a completed action.
3.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — to do, to act, to make

4.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
4.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

5.meaning: To/against our gods — the deities (here false ones) belonging to a group. A feminine plural noun governed by the preposition 'bi-' (with/to/against), carrying the possessive 'our'.
5.grammar: Noun (broken plural of 'ilāh', god) governed by the preposition 'bi-', which puts it in the genitive (the -i before the suffix). The attached -nā means 'our'. The preposition gives the sense 'with/to/against our gods'.
5.root: ء-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, deity; that which is worshipped

6.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
6.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

7.meaning: An emphatic 'truly/surely' joined to the preposition min ('from, among, of') — conveying 'surely (one) of / among', stressing belonging to a group.
7.grammar: Two particles. 'la-' is the emphatic prefix adding certainty (often paired with inna). 'min' is a preposition meaning 'from/among/of' and puts the noun after it into the genitive case. Its final -a here is a connecting vowel used before the definite article 'al-'.

8.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
8.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.
8.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — darkness; wrongdoing, injustice

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'we heard / we listened' — the act of perceiving sound or a message, often carrying the further nuance of heeding or taking in what was said.
2.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The attached ending -nā marks the subject as 'we', so the action is something a group did and finished: 'we heard'.

3.meaning: A young man, a youth in the prime of life; can also denote a brave or noble young servant. An indefinite singular noun whose underlying weak final letter shows up as the '-an' ending.

parts.en: indefinite ending on a weak-final noun

3.grammar: Singular noun ending in an original weak letter (yāʾ/alif maqṣūra). In its indefinite form it takes the nunation '-an'; because the final root letter is weak, the case distinctions collapse into this single fixed ending.
3.root: ف-ت-ي (f-t-y) — youth, the vigour and nobility of young manhood

4.meaning: He mentions them, makes mention of them, speaks of them; also 'he remembers/recalls them'. A present-tense verb of mentioning or remembering, with the attached object 'them'.
4.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the 'ya-' prefix marks 'he', and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, denoting an ongoing or habitual action. The attached -hum is the object 'them'.
4.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to mention, recall, remember, call to mind

5.meaning: He/it is called or said to be; the passive 'is named/spoken'. A present-tense passive verb meaning that something is said or a name is given, with no actor specified.
5.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular. The 'yu-' prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks the passive ('is …'), and the final -u marks the ordinary indicative present. The doer is left unnamed; the focus is on the action being done.
5.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter; to call (by a name)

6.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
6.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

7.meaning: A proper noun: Abraham (Ibrāhīm), the patriarch and prophet, exalted as an upright monotheist and 'friend of Allah'.
7.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence. Because it is a foreign proper name, it is 'diptote' — it does not take the indefinite 'n' sound (tanwīn) that ordinary nouns would.

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'bring!', 'come with!', 'produce!'. From the verb 'to come'; in this pattern with the preposition 'bi-' it means to bring or produce something. Preceded by 'fa-', it reads 'then bring / so produce'.
2.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector signalling a consequence ('then …'). The middle piece is the bare imperative stem of the verb 'to come' (singular '(i)ti'); the '-ū' ending then marks a masculine plural audience ('you all, bring!'). Commands have no case ending. The initial 'i'-sound is a helping vowel that lets the word begin smoothly.
2.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (with bi-) to bring, to produce

3.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
3.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
4.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').
4.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

5.meaning: Eyes — the organs of sight. A plural noun in the genitive form, often appearing in possessive or prepositional constructions ('… of the eyes', 'before the eyes').
5.grammar: Noun, broken plural of 'ʿayn' (eye), in the genitive case. The -i ending typically links it to a following noun ('… OF …') or marks it as the object of a preposition.
5.root: ع-ي-ن (ʿ-y-n) — eye; spring of water; the essence of a thing

6.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
6.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
6.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

7.meaning: 'So that they may / perhaps they will.' A particle expressing hope, expectation, or purpose, fused with the pronoun 'them'; it introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

7.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps, in the hope that, so that') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), which serves as its subject. Laʿalla belongs to a family of particles that put a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -hum is that fixed object form. It conveys hope or an intended purpose rather than certainty.
7.root: — (particle with pronoun; no root)

8.meaning: 'they bear witness / testify' — a group giving firm testimony or attesting to the truth of something.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending means 'they' (masculine plural). The -ūna ending marks the ordinary, unrestricted present tense for a plural subject ('they bear witness / do testify').
8.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, testify, be present

1.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'they said' or 'they spoke,' attributing an utterance to a group of three or more (grammatically masculine or mixed).
1.grammar: Past-tense verb in the third-person masculine plural. The stem qāl- carries a long ā (from a weak middle root letter), and the plural subject is marked by the wāw vowel -ū fused onto it ('they'). The alif written after the wāw is silent — a purely orthographic spelling convention with no pronunciation.

2.meaning: 'Did You …?' — the questioning particle 'a' (introducing a yes/no question) joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (single male): 'Was it you who …?'
2.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' (turns a statement into a yes/no question) attached to the detached subject pronoun 'anta' ('you', masculine singular). Fronting the pronoun emphasizes the doer: 'Was it YOU who …?'

3.meaning: You did / you did it / you acted — the basic verb faʿala means to do, make, or perform an act. The -ta ending pins the doer as 'you.'
3.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb. The suffix -ta marks the subject as second-person-masculine-singular, 'you did.' Past-tense verbs of this kind attach the doer as an ending rather than a prefix.
3.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — to do, make, act, perform

4.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
4.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

5.meaning: To/against our gods — the deities (here false ones) belonging to a group. A feminine plural noun governed by the preposition 'bi-' (with/to/against), carrying the possessive 'our'.
5.grammar: Noun (broken plural of 'ilāh', god) governed by the preposition 'bi-', which puts it in the genitive (the -i before the suffix). The attached -nā means 'our'. The preposition gives the sense 'with/to/against our gods'.
5.root: ء-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, deity; that which is worshipped

6.meaning: O Ibrahim (Abraham): the prophet's name addressed directly with the call-word 'O'.
6.grammar: A vocative (direct-address) phrase: yā is the call-particle 'O'. The final -u marks the noun being called by name. As a proper name it has no root.
6.root: — (proper name)

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

3.meaning: He did it; he performed/committed the act. A simple past-tense verb of doing, with the attached object pronoun 'it'.
3.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he did', a completed action. The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'it/him' (masculine singular).
3.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — to do, act, perform, make

4.meaning: A combination of 'their greatest / eldest / chief one' — the adjective 'big, great, senior' used as a noun, plus 'their'.
4.grammar: The adjective kabīr ('great, senior') on the faʿīl pattern, used as a noun, with the -u ending marking the nominative (subject) case, joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('their'): 'their eldest/chief'.
4.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, seniority

5.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
5.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

6.meaning: So ask them; put a question to them, request information from them. A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group, prefixed with 'so/then' and carrying the object 'them'.
6.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you'; the long '-ū' is the plural-command ending, telling a group to do the action. The prefixed 'fa-' means 'so/then'; the attached -hum is the object 'them'.
6.root: س-ء-ل (s-ʾ-l) — to ask, question, request, inquire

7.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
7.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

8.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
8.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

9.meaning: They speak, articulate, utter intelligible words; the capacity for meaningful speech. A present-tense verb of speaking in the third-person masculine plural.
9.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural: the 'ya-' prefix plus the '-ūna' ending together mean 'they (men) …', and the retained final '-na' marks the ordinary (indicative) present of an ongoing or habitual action.
9.root: ن-ط-ق (n-ṭ-q) — to speak, articulate, give voice to intelligible words

1.meaning: So they returned, went back, came back (to a place, a person, or a prior state). A past-tense verb of returning in the third-person masculine plural, prefixed with 'so/then'.
1.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine plural: the '-ū' ending means 'they (men) did' the action, completed. The prefixed 'fa-' means 'so/then', marking sequence. (The final alif after the '-ū' is silent, written but not pronounced.)
1.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — to return, go back, revert

2.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
2.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

3.meaning: Themselves / their own selves — the noun nafs ('self, soul, person, inner being') joined to a pronoun 'their'. Used reflexively it means 'their own selves' and conveys the inmost self, the seat of desires and the person as a whole.
3.grammar: The plural noun anfus ('selves') carries the genitive -i ending followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The genitive marks the noun as governed by a preposition or joined to a preceding word; -him makes it 'their selves'.
3.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath, inner being

4.meaning: '…so / then they said.' Combines the connector 'so/then' (showing result or sequence) with a past-tense verb of speaking, third person plural — a completed act of saying by a group.
4.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb prefixed with 'fa-' ('so/then'), which links it to what precedes as a result or next step. The '-ū' ending (with silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural).
4.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

5.meaning: 'Indeed you (plural)' — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed, surely'), which strongly affirms and stresses the statement that follows, fused with the attached pronoun 'you (all)'. Inna has no single English word; it functions to underline certainty.
5.grammar: Inna is an emphasising particle that introduces and strengthens a sentence; grammatically it places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative-like role of its 'subject'. The attached -kum is the masculine plural object/possessive pronoun 'you (all)'. Together: 'indeed you (all)…'.

6.meaning: You (a group of males) — the detached/standalone pronoun for a plural 'you', used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own. The final short vowel is a connecting vowel before a following word.
6.grammar: Independent (standalone) personal pronoun, second-person masculine plural, 'you all'. It does not attach to another word; it stands alone to emphasize or identify the subject. The final '-u' is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before the next word.

7.meaning: The wrongdoers; those who do wrong, act unjustly, or place things where they do not belong. The underlying image is one who oppresses, transgresses limits, and deals unjustly with others or with themselves.
7.grammar: An active participle (the doer of the action) made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case, the form used when the word functions as the doer of a verb or the subject of a sentence.
7.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

2.meaning: They were turned upside down / set head-downward; figuratively, they were made to relapse or reverse into confusion. A past-tense passive verb in the third-person masculine plural, with no actor named.

parts.en: they were turned upside down / overturned

2.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) passive verb, third-person masculine plural: the internal vowel pattern (u-i) marks the passive 'were …', and the '-ū' ending means 'they (men)'. The doer is unstated; the focus is on what was done to them. (The final alif is silent.)
2.root: ن-ك-س (n-k-s) — to turn upside down, invert, reverse, cause to relapse

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

4.meaning: Their heads — the head as the topmost part of the body. A plural noun in the genitive form with the attached possessive 'their' (a group of males).
4.grammar: Noun, broken plural of 'raʾs' (head), in the genitive case (the -i before the suffix). The attached -him means 'their' (masculine plural). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links the noun to a preceding one.
4.root: ر-ء-س (r-ʾ-s) — head; chief, top, the principal part

5.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
5.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

6.meaning: You (singular) knew / have come to know; the speaker's addressee possesses this knowledge.
6.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -ta ending marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you' knew).
6.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowing, knowledge

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: These / those — a plural demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things. Its core sense is the near demonstrative 'these', but it is very commonly rendered 'those' in translation when the group it points to has already been described or named rather than being physically present.
8.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, used for a group of either gender. Its base value is near-deixis ('these'), built from an attention-drawing prefix 'hā-' ('lo!, here') plus the base 'ulāʾi'. In practice it is often translated 'those' when the referent is already mentioned or understood rather than literally nearby. Its form is fixed and does not change for grammatical case; it points to a group rather than naming it.

9.meaning: They speak, articulate, utter intelligible words; the capacity for meaningful speech. A present-tense verb of speaking in the third-person masculine plural.
9.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural: the 'ya-' prefix plus the '-ūna' ending together mean 'they (men) …', and the retained final '-na' marks the ordinary (indicative) present of an ongoing or habitual action.
9.root: ن-ط-ق (n-ṭ-q) — to speak, articulate, give voice to intelligible words

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: Do you then worship…? — a pointed, reproachful question about worshipping. A present-tense verb of worship addressed to a group, opened by the question particle and the connector, expressing astonishment or rebuke.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all worship'): the 'ta-' prefix plus '-ūna' ending mark 'you (men) …', with the retained '-na' showing the ordinary (indicative) present. The opening 'a-' makes it a question and the 'fa-' adds 'then', so together it is a rhetorical, reproachful 'Do you then worship…?'
2.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, devote oneself in obedience

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
3.root: — (preposition)

4.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
4.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
4.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

8.meaning: "It benefits you / profits you" — to be of use or advantage to someone, with an attached plural 'you' as the one benefited.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb: the ya- prefix marks a masculine 'he/it' as the doer and the -u ending marks the plain present/future indicative ('benefits / will benefit'). The attached -kum is the object 'you' (masculine plural).
8.root: ن-ف-ع (n-f-ʿ) — benefit, profit, be useful

9.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
9.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'
9.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — thing, to will

10.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
10.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

11.meaning: "It harms you / injures you" — the act of causing harm, hurt, or damage to a group of people.
